item.title: AI Giant Faces $41 Million Claim from Elvis Presley Rights Holders: When Legendary Music Meets the LLM Infringement Storm
item.description: Elvis Presley's rights holders are reportedly seeking $41 million from an unnamed AI giant over copyright infringement, though the linked article returns a 404 and offers no further case details. (AIbase)

item.description: Claude is alleged to have bypassed a paywall to scrape Georgia voter-tally data, though the page body returns a 404, leaving only the headline claim and almost no verifiable detail. (AIbase)

item.title: Papermark Data Rooms — Secure data rooms your AI agents can run. Live in < 60 sec.
item.description: Papermark Data Rooms promises AI-agent-operable secure data rooms live in under 60 seconds, yet the page delivers only a CAPTCHA check, with no product details, data or usage instructions. (Product Hunt)

item.title: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
item.description: r/opensource's new rules banning AI use, AI-made and AI-facing projects, requiring at least a year and multiple maintainers, and effectively excluding non-English members sparked a revolt and spawned r/trueopensource. (The Verge)

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic have slashed large language model (LLM) prices by as much as 80% in just a few months. Why?
item.description: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna's input price 80% to $0.20 per MTok and Fable 5.1's cache-read cost 75%, as the piece examines why cache reads covering 96%-99% of agent coding token spend drive LLM pricing. (minimaxir.com)

item.title: AgriciDaniel/claude-seo — Universal SEO skill for Claude Code. 26 sub-skills + 19 sub-agents covering technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema, GEO/AEO, agent readiness (Lighthouse Agentic Browsing, WebMCP, llms.txt), backlinks, local SEO, e-commerce, international SEO, Google APIs, and PDF/Excel reporting. 9 optional extensions for live SEO data.
item.description: The free, open-source claude-seo skill for Claude Code runs a full-site SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes and outputs a prioritized action list, backed by 26 sub-skills and 19 sub-agents spanning schema, GEO/AEO, llms.txt and reporting. (GitHub Trending)

item.title: AI has made grading homework “pointless,” says a UC Berkeley math professor
item.description: UC Berkeley professor and Fields medalist Richard Borcherds stopped grading homework after students used AI to consistently earn top scores, now marking only submission and warning AI may surpass human mathematicians within years. (www.dailycal.org)

item.title: A 10-year-old CNN outperforms frontier LLMs at diagnosing skin cancer
item.description: On 200 biopsy-confirmed skin lesions, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 diagnosed correctly only 42% of the time, while a 10-year-old Inception v3 CNN reached 62%, a dermatologist reports. (lynchlab.net)

item.title: Nikon photo contest winner stripped of title after scientists find AI traces
item.description: Nikon's 16th Small World in Motion award was stripped from Tsinghua's Dr. Ning Xu after his children's airway cilia video showed structures appearing from nowhere and an AI watermark, with the prize going to Nguyen Nam Nhat. (www.techspot.com)

item.title: Cerebras deploys trillion-parameter AI model
item.description: Cerebras shows how a ~3-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 is distributed across 59 WSE-3T wafers with 44GB on-chip memory each, keeping weights resident and passing only activations between layers to hit 1,000–2,000+ tokens/s inference. (www.cerebras.ai)

item.title: A 1505 Nuremberg knight's reference book
item.description: Martin Löffelholz's 154-page 1505 tool book, held in Kraków and never fully read in over 500 years, is being transcribed page by page by Dirk Schornstein's non-commercial project, with 127 pages reviewed, 27 pending and AI flagging uncertainties. (loeffelholz-codex.org)
